items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: I played with Buddy P.T. for a good while. While our jobs was mostly out of town, he used to go to Buckaloozie and go through Mississippi, just get jobs out of those places.

ctx.x: Well, I'll tell you the truth. I never did. I ain't never even hoid him to play with a man. Mm-hmm. I never hoid him to play. I couldn't tell you that. Where were you brought up anyway? Here in the city. Well, we'll start the beginning. Where were you falling exactly? I was falling right down here in the Sempern Hall. Ellen and Priya. Ellen and Priya? It's not far from him. And where have you lived? Did you say that most of your life? No. Well, I don't remember that address. But the next place that I remember was…

Reel 2, Albert Burbank, January the 4th, 1962. You say you will work with many bands, huh? Yeah. Such as? Such as Buddy P.T., Kid Thomas. When did you work with Thomas? Well, that's way back, but I just can't remember. Before the break and after? Why do you remember? I don't remember if it was before or after. But I worked with him for a pretty good while, I guess for about a year or so. He did. I didn't know that. He's waiting across the room. He had a job on weekends. I played with Buddy P.T. for a good while.…
Well, who's selling tickets then? Is Buddy selling tickets himself?

items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1959-03-18
items.q: I played with Buddy Petit. At the time I played with Buddy Petit, he had an eight-piece band.

ctx.x: For a while. Did you ever play with Buddy Petit? Oh, yeah.
I played with Buddy Petit. At the time I played with Buddy Petit, he had an eight-piece band. And he used to go out of town, all around Muggaloosa. Mm-hmm.
How many, you say, eight pieces that have two trumpets or sax? Oh, yeah.
